Denis Murphy’s Polka

In around 1958 fiddler Jackie Roche recorded this as “The Connemara Polka”. He paired it with “The Munster Polka” which is well known in Scotland as “My Love She’s but a Lassie Yet”.

Denis Murphy’s, X:8

Ted McGraw calls this Flaherty’s Favourite, and he got it from a Copley 78 by Martin Flaherty’s Orchestra. The B part’s 4th and 7th bars are quite distinct from the “main line” tune, but it feels like it should go here rather than as its own tune entry.

↳ Posted by NfldWhistler on September 6th, 2023.

Denis Murphy’s polka (S: Denis Murphy & Johnny O’Leary)

An approximation of the fantastic wild version of this polka as played by the fiddle-accordion duo of Denis Murphy & Johnny O’Leary on RTÉ 183 CD: Music From Sliabh Luachra (1995).

Given how bland this tune is often played in sessions around the world, it’s good to sometimes slow down these recordings and listen closely to all the creativity bursting out of these musical giants. Bonus inspiration points guaranteed!

P.S.: And yes, that weird-looking ornamented triplet is actually a full-blown roll condensed into the polka beat (love them).

↳ Posted by Bregolas on January 29th, 2024.

Denis Murphy’s polka (Denis Murphy & Johnny O’Leary simplified)

A simplified version of Denis Murphy’s polka based on the version from Music From Sliabh Luachra with a little Denis-Murphish twist thrown at the end.

↳ Posted by Bregolas on January 29th, 2024.

Sweeney’s Polka (Kerry Polkas)

It is one of the first tunes I encountered, in a book called “Irish Melodies for Soprano Recorder” by Joachim Johow. We play it regularly in our sessions at O’Malleys in Groningen. I was surprised it’s not on this site yet or possibly it is but I just couldn’t find it. If the latter is the case please move my version to the appropriate tune.

↳ Posted by Paul Joosten on January 12th, 2025.
